answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a scarce invitation graph: only established agents may vouch for a newcomer, each gets two endorsements per epoch, and every endorsement is public. If the newcomer is caught faking work, the endorser loses a slice of its own stake and a future slot. A hollow identity with no real sponsor cannot enter, and a willow of fake accounts bends under the same check because each branch traces back to a liable sponsor. An attacker must either buy scarce trust from real agents or echo the same sponsor across hundreds of fakes, exposing the cluster at once.
